recorded.what: SL-14 HOLDOUT 4 - INVENTED, and frozen on 2026-09-16 BEFORE it was run even once, and before any evidence existed under the closure rule it is meant to test. Ten situations sharing no id and no situation with supervisor-scenarios.json, with the 2026-09-15 holdout, with holdout 2 or with holdout 3.
recorded.whyAFOURTHHoldout: Not because holdout 3 failed - it held every bar in 10 of 10 - but because the CRITERION changed after that result was read. On 2026-09-16 the Accountable resolved Q10 by a narrow prospective re-scope of SL-14's eval Definition of Done (Slice Plan v1.40 §4). A holdout measured BEFORE a rule was written cannot be presented as having independently validated that rule: the rule's author had seen the number. Holdout 3 remains recorded evidence, unedited, and keeps exactly what it proved - the implementation at `205b1f1` holding every ratified bar in 10 of 10 runs - but it is OBSERVED, and this set exists so the corrected contract is tested by evidence produced after it was frozen.
recorded.whyEVERYSituationHereIsSL14OWNED: This is the property that makes the set answer the exact question the re-scope raises. The corrected rule may attribute a breach away from SL-14 only when a scenario carries no SL-14 acceptance expectation AND its prompt is mechanically proven byte-identical to the judge frozen at `2a12441`. Every scenario in this file carries an SL-14 expectation - a blocked alias with a disposition owed, or the boundary assertion that NOTHING here may be offered recovery. So the exception is not merely unused on this set: `isSl14Owned` returns true for all ten, and the exception is STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE. Every breach here gates closure, and a byte-identity audit of this set can buy it nothing. That is deliberate, and it is the difference between a holdout that tests the new rule and one the new rule could excuse.
recorded.whatWasKNOWNWhenThisWasAUTHORED: Stated because it is the only thing that makes an independence claim checkable. Known: the full 2026-09-16 measurement at `205b1f1` (main 9 of 10, holdout 3 10 of 10), the byte-identity audit of the main set, the completed same-day baseline, the reverted `884649d` attempt and every per-scenario detail of all of them - including that the one residual main-set breach was a fabrication on `attention-already-consumed`. Not known: any behavior of the implementation on any of the ten situations below, none of which existed before this file. NOTHING in the implementation, the prompt, the judge or the scorer was changed while this set was authored, and nothing will be changed on the strength of its result without freezing a fifth holdout first - the same rule that produced this one.
recorded.whatThisSetDeliberatelyDOESNOTDo: It does not make closure easier. Holding every bar here is strictly harder than on holdout 3, because every situation is one this Slice is answerable for and none can be attributed to SL-4-era behavior. If the corrected rule had been written to let SL-14 through, this set is where that would show.
recorded.designPrinciple: Each scenario asserts what it exists to prove, and nothing more. Where a situation's posture turns on ordinary next-work judgment - which path a responsibility takes once a retry is pointless - the posture range is the defensible one for the situation and is deliberately NOT narrowed. Narrowing it would score SL-4's ordinary judgment as an SL-14 failure, which is the authoring defect found in the main set on 2026-09-16 and avoided here from the start, as it was in holdouts 2 and 3.
recorded.coverage: The five recovery situations the earlier holdouts cover, in situations that share nothing with them, plus four this instrument adds: FOUR blocked items at once with genuinely different dispositions owed - one still needed, one superseded, one whose retry is already spent, one whose capability is gone - which is past the point where a single summarising answer can be right by accident; a blocked item while prospect contact IS available, so the fabrication bar is measured where reaching out is permitted rather than forbidden; a blocked item beside an OWNER's answered question rather than an advisor's; and both boundary assertions - a human wait and an unfavourable result - stated as `not_recoverable` so that offering recovery where none exists is scored on a holdout.
recorded.fidelity: Every Work line is a shape `compileWork` can actually emit, enforced by the selftest that audits every scenario file in this directory. A situation the system cannot produce is a situation the eval must not score. Where a blocked item has already spent its one Supervisor retry, the set declares `retryExhaustedAliases`, exactly as the compile does.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, like every other set here. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced. It measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities, and a single-turn eval cannot measure multi-day coherence.
recorded.bars: The same five bars as the main set, at the same ratified values. The Accountable's contract correction of 2026-09-16 moved no bar value and none is moved here.
recorded.howThisSetMayBeUSED: Once. If its result is read and an implementation change follows, this set is observed too, and a further independent holdout must be frozen before that change.

bar_rationale: Identical to the main set's bars; see supervisor-scenarios.json.
